issues.description: Audio packetization complects framing concern with the transport's send loop
issues.detail: The fixed_audio_packet_size buffer is glued onto _write_frame, mixing three concerns: serialization, framing/packetization, and transport send. The serializer produces a value (PCM bytes), but the transport mutates a place (_audio_send_buffer) to reshape that value. A simple decomposition would be a pure function chunk(buffer, payload, size) -> (chunks, remainder), or a small Packetizer component owned by the serializer (which already knows about Vonage's framing requirements). Right now Vonage's protocol requirement leaks into a generic FastAPI transport flag.

issues.description: Packetization couples to bytes payloads only, silently dropping other payload types
issues.detail: When fixed_audio_packet_size is set and payload is bytes, the code buffers and returns early; when payload is anything else (str JSON), it falls through to send. This is an implicit type-dispatch hidden in a flag. The 'identity' of what this transport sends is now conditional on payload type and a config flag entangled together. A serializer that returns mixed text/binary while fixed_audio_packet_size is set has subtle behavior that is not documented and not obvious from the call site.

issues.description: Buffer is place-oriented mutable state with implicit time semantics on interruption
issues.detail: _audio_send_buffer is a bytearray mutated across calls. The InterruptionFrame handler clears it, but there is no explicit model of 'what audio is in flight, what is pending, what has been dropped.' The 'value' of the audio stream and the 'identity' of the buffer are conflated. If two coroutines ever raced _write_frame and process_frame(InterruptionFrame), the clear and the extend could interleave. State the time model explicitly, or push the buffer behind a single owner with clear semantics.

issues.description: Final partial buffer on stream end is silently dropped
issues.detail: When the stream ends with fewer than packet_bytes remaining in the buffer, the remainder sits there forever (or is cleared on the next interruption). There is no flush/zero-pad path. For a 20ms-frame protocol like Vonage, a tail of <20ms is probably fine to drop, but the decision should be explicit — either pad with silence, or document that tail audio under one packet is dropped. Right now the time semantics of 'end of utterance' are accidental.

issues.description: Resampler is a place with hidden state but no reset across sessions
issues.detail: create_stream_resampler() returns a stateful object used across the whole serializer lifetime. Vonage event 'websocket:cleared' and pipeline interruption both indicate a discontinuity, but neither resets _input_resampler or _output_resampler. Stateful resamplers typically carry filter history; replaying that history across a discontinuity produces audible artifacts at boundaries. The value (audio chunk in) and the identity (resampler instance) are intertwined with no explicit time model for 'when does history matter.'

issues.description: DTMF digit extraction reaches into two shapes, encoding an undocumented either/or
issues.detail: `digit = message.get("digit") or message.get("dtmf", {}).get("digit")` quietly handles two payload shapes without naming them or citing where the ambiguity comes from. This is incidental complexity created by uncertainty about the wire format. Either pin the format from Vonage docs and handle one shape, or name both shapes as known variants in a comment with a link. Right now the data model of a DTMF event is implicit in a defensive expression.

issues.description: InputParams.sample_rate override is a value that depends on identity-of-StartFrame
issues.detail: self._sample_rate starts at 0 and is only set in setup(). If serialize/deserialize were ever called before setup (a real risk in a generic Frame pipeline), the resampler would be asked to resample to rate 0. There is no guard. A simpler shape: make sample_rate part of an immutable config constructed at setup time, and refuse to operate before it exists, so the 'is this serializer ready' question has one answer instead of being implicit in field values.

issues.description: The packetization feature is named generically but exists for one protocol
issues.detail: `fixed_audio_packet_size` lives on the generic FastAPIWebsocketParams, but the only motivation is Vonage's Audio Connector contract. This is easy (one flag, drop it in) but not simple (now every user of FastAPIWebsocketTransport must understand a Vonage-shaped framing knob). If Vonage's serializer required this framing, the framing should arguably live with the serializer (e.g. a serializer-side `packet_size` and a generic transport contract that 'serializer output is already framed correctly'). That keeps each concern in one place.

review.summary: The Vonage serializer itself is reasonably close to simple — it is mostly a pure transform between two data shapes, with a couple of stateful resamplers and a small JSON event dispatch. The packetization change in FastAPIWebsocketTransport is the place where this PR complects concerns: serialization, framing, and transport are mixed in one method, with a mutable place (the send buffer) whose time semantics are only partly defined (cleared on interruption, never flushed at end, never guarded across types of payload). The framing logic is a pure function over (buffer, payload, packet_size); pulling it into a tiny packetizer (ideally owned by the serializer that needs it) would separate the concerns and let the transport stay generic. The question that should have been asked first: whose responsibility is wire-level audio framing — the transport, or the serializer that knows the wire protocol — and where do value, identity, and time live for the in-flight audio buffer?
